rem Last digits of divisors
rem https://projecteuler.net/problem=474

use numbers
use sequences
use bits
use io
use cli

fun Unit permutation Domain
  Units = Domain .units
  Places = Domain .places
  Modulus = Domain .modulus
  return Places (Units * Unit mod Modulus)
end

arg N integer = 1000000
arg D integer = 65432

rem D = 2^a 5^b T with a, b below its
rem K digits: a divisor ending in D
rem has exactly 2^a 5^b, and its rest
rem is the unit T mod M = 10^K / (2^a
rem 5^b). Count the products of the
rem other prime powers by residue.
Md = 10000000000000061
K = D text len
T = D
Al = 0
Be = 0
for T mod 2 equal 0
  T //= 2
  Al += 1
end
for T mod 5 equal 0
  T //= 5
  Be += 1
end
M = 10 ** K // (2 ** Al * 5 ** Be)
Pr = primes to N array
rem Exponents of the primes in N!.
E = Pr * 0
Pk = Pr
for Pk at most N any
  E += N // Pk
  Lo = Pk at most N
  Pk = Lo choose (Pk * Pr) Pk
end
E5 = 0
if N at least 5
  E5 = E 2
end
Answer = 0
if Al at most E 0 and Be at most E5
  Rs = 0 till M copy
  Cp = Rs gcd 10 equal 1
  Us = Rs (Cp indices)
  Nu = Us len
  Ps = Rs * 0
  Ps Us = 0 till Us len copy
  Domain = record
    .units = Us
    .places = Ps
    .modulus = M
  end
  A = Us * 0
  A (Ps 1) = 1
  rem Exponent j of p moves count from
  rem x to x p^j: the sum of e + 1
  rem shifts by p^-1, built by binary
  rem doubling. Sums stay below 2^63
  rem for 8 doublings between mods.
  Fr = Pr mod 2 equal 1
  Fr = Fr and (Pr mod 5 not equal 0)
  Bd = 0
  for I in Fr indices
    Pv = (Pr I) (Nu - 1) M powmod
    R1 = Pv permutation Domain
    Bt = E I + 1 binary
    Sm = A
    Cu = 1
    for J in 1 till Bt len
      W = Pv Cu M powmod
      Sm += Sm (W permutation Domain)
      Cu *= 2
      Bd += 1
      if Bt J equal "1"
        Sm = A + Sm R1
        Cu += 1
        Bd += 1
      end
      if Bd at least 8
        Sm = Sm mod Md
        Bd = 0
      end
    end
    A = Sm
  end
  Answer = (A (Ps (T mod M))) mod Md
end
Answer print

rem Last digits of divisors
rem https://projecteuler.net/problem=474

use numbers
use sequences
use bits
use io
use cli

arg Block integer = 128

fun Units permutation_table Modulus
  Count = Units len
  Table = array shape Count Count fill 0
  for Start in 0 till Count by Block
    Stop = Start + Block min Count
    Rows = Start till Stop
    Height = Rows len
    Column = (Units Rows) reshape Height 1
    Keys = Column * Units mod Modulus
    Table Rows = Keys * 2 // 5
  end
  return Table
end

arg N integer = 1000000
arg D integer = 65432

rem D = 2^a 5^b T with a, b below its
rem K digits: a divisor ending in D
rem has exactly 2^a 5^b, and its rest
rem is the unit T mod M = 10^K / (2^a
rem 5^b). Count the products of the
rem other prime powers by residue.
Md = 10000000000000061
K = D text len
T = D
Al = 0
Be = 0
for T mod 2 equal 0
  T //= 2
  Al += 1
end
for T mod 5 equal 0
  T //= 5
  Be += 1
end
M = 10 ** K // (2 ** Al * 5 ** Be)
Pr = primes to N array
rem Exponents of the primes in N!.
E = Pr * 0
Pk = Pr
for Pk at most N any
  E += N // Pk
  Lo = Pk at most N
  Pk = Lo choose (Pk * Pr) Pk
end
E5 = 0
if N at least 5
  E5 = E 2
end
Answer = 0
if Al at most E 0 and Be at most E5
  Rs = 0 till M copy
  Cp = Rs gcd 10 equal 1
  Us = Rs (Cp indices)
  Nu = Us len
  rem Tx w i: position of u_i times
  rem the unit at position w.
  Tx = Us permutation_table M
  A = Us * 0
  A 0 = 1
  rem Exponent j of p moves count from
  rem x to x p^j: the sum of e + 1
  rem shifts by p^-1, built by binary
  rem doubling. Sums stay below 2^63
  rem for 8 doublings between mods.
  Fr = Pr mod 2 equal 1
  Fr = Fr and (Pr mod 5 not equal 0)
  Bd = 0
  for I in Fr indices
    Pv = (Pr I) (Nu - 1) M powmod
    R1' = Tx (Pv * 2 // 5)
    Bt = E I + 1 binary
    Sm = A
    Cu = 1
    for J in 1 till Bt len
      W = Pv Cu M powmod
      Sm += Sm (Tx (W * 2 // 5))
      Cu *= 2
      Bd += 1
      if Bt J equal "1"
        Sm = A + Sm R1
        Cu += 1
        Bd += 1
      end
      if Bd at least 8
        Sm = Sm mod Md
        Bd = 0
      end
    end
    A = Sm
  end
  Remainder = T mod M
  Answer = (A (Remainder * 2 // 5)) mod Md
end
Answer print
